technical.lead: FMRB EO classified-annex day 4: CISA Director files second submission, T-2 to May 22
technical.body: The Frontier Model Review Board executive order rolled into Tuesday with the ten-business-day classified-annex response clock advancing to its fourth calendar day, the deadline now at T-minus-two business days to the Friday May 22 expiry. A Tuesday Lawfare procedural note reported the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency Director's office filing the second substantive submission against the Senate Cyber Subcommittee's classified-annex follow-up question set, joining Monday's first submission from NIST Director Locascio's office, with the remaining six witnesses confirming response drafts will land inside the deadline window. A Tuesday Just Security analysis restated that the classified-annex question set is the last remaining open procedural gate, observed that two of eight witnesses now on record inside the first two business days is on the steeper response cadence the eight-witness slate had targeted, and confirmed White House OSTP holding the line that the order remains in interagency review with no signing window before May 22. The House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Communications and Technology converted Monday's markup-scheduling decision into a calendar entry for the parallel 30-day technical-review joint-resolution draft, with the markup notice posted Tuesday morning for the new week's first formal House-track movement since the order's signing window opened.

technical.lead: Cerebras Tuesday follow-through: $185-235 band holds, MS upside prob ticks to 42%
technical.body: Cerebras CBRS opened Tuesday with the market's follow-through session after Monday's first re-rating of the four-consecutive-day consolidation base, holding the Friday $198.60 close as the reference anchor with the May 21 Alphabet analyst day stepping to T-minus-two calendar days. A Tuesday BEAMSTART note reported the five-desk analyst spread carrying into the second trading day of the week unchanged from Monday's open — Bernstein's $185 Market-Perform floor, Morgan Stanley's $192 target with the upside-scenario probability nudging to 42 percent, Wells Fargo Securities Buy at $208, Jefferies Outperform at $225, and UBS Neutral at $205 — leaving the stock bracketed inside the same roughly $185-to-$235 band, with institutional-buyside cumulative net position edging up to roughly 38 percent of float as desks added incremental long exposure. A Tuesday Datacenter Dynamics wire reported the Saudi Aramco Digital MoU close holding its late-Q2 2026 window and the Saudi PIF contingent-secondary discussion now into its second week of the 10-21 day execution window, with the desk preview cohort treating Tuesday as the first session in the analyst-day run-up where directional positioning typically firms ahead of a Mag-7 print catalyst.

technical.lead: n8n CVE-2026-21858 day-19 scan: ~1,395 exposed; CISA directive in first operating day
technical.body: The Shadowserver day-nineteen n8n CVE-2026-21858 (Ni8mare) Tuesday scan extended Monday's resumed weekday descent as the May 21 federal-civilian remediation deadline reached T-minus-two business days. Internet-exposed pre-1.121.0 instances continued the descent to approximately 1,395 (down from Monday's 1,640), with the US cohort easing to roughly 410 and the India cohort to approximately 215, and the residual long-tail unpatched share falling to about 10 percent as the federal-civilian directive's compliance window closed in. Censys honeypot telemetry reported exploitation attempts holding at approximately 1.7x baseline at the Tuesday 09:00 UTC mark — the post-weekend weekday operating tempo carrying flat into the second business-week day — consistent with commodity-tier exploit-kit volume settling rather than ramping ahead of the deadline. CISA's Tuesday KEV-catalog note restated that the May 21 federal-civilian remediation deadline now sits at T-minus-two business days, and CSO Online reported that the CISA federal-civilian operational directive published Monday morning is now into its first full operating day, with the eleven-CVE Trail of Bits agent-loader taxonomy compliance window keyed to Friday May 22 and federal-civilian operators reporting incremental remediation completions against the catalogued patterns.

technical.lead: Mistral Workflows day-19: Sweden Skatteverket lifts central-government cohort to 9
technical.body: Mistral AI Workflows day-nineteen Tuesday update advanced the sovereign-cloud central-government reference count to nine, with Monday's Netherlands Belastingdienst addition now joined by Sweden Skatteverket, and the cross-orchestrator interop matrix continuing to hold its first-week-of-June general-availability target. Mistral's Tuesday note reported the Swedish tax authority joining the prior eight references — France DGFiP, Germany Bundesagentur fuer Arbeit, UK HMRC, Italy Agenzia delle Entrate, Spain AEAT, Portugal Autoridade Tributaria, Belgium FOD Financien, and Netherlands Belastingdienst — as the second fresh central-government estate selection of the business week; paid Workflows tenancy edged to approximately 408 enterprise customers and the daily-execution count to roughly 7.5M. Mistral confirmed the five-vendor cross-orchestrator interop matrix — Codex CLI plus Claude Code 3.0 plus Mistral Workflows plus Azure AI Foundry plus Vertex AI Agent Governance Center plus Amazon Bedrock Agent Registry — holds its first-week-of-June general-availability target, shipping the five-surface signed-checkpoint plus manifest-allowlist plus workflow-state plus intermediate-state-serializer plus nested-dependency-resolution canonicalization mitigation set as a default with support for all fifteen-jurisdiction Indo-Pacific cohort tenant-policy field schemas. A Tuesday InfoQ note reported the interop-matrix conformance test suite holding green across all five vendors for a second consecutive weekday with no schema-drift regression, and noted the suite now includes a training-surface checkpoint-provenance check folded in from Monday's arxiv extension.

technical.lead: Tuesday arxiv 2605.07735 extends loader verification to tenant-policy attestation
technical.body: A Tuesday arxiv release (2605.07735) opened the business week's second research day by extending the loader-verification line one further surface — from Monday's training-pipeline checkpoint-provenance extension to a tenant-policy-attestation surface, presenting a verification model that binds Monday's training-surface signed-checkpoint provenance chain to a per-tenant policy-attestation manifest covering the fifteen-jurisdiction reciprocity perimeter's tenant-policy field schemas. The paper, positioned as a third extension of the consolidated 2605.07241 framework after its 2605.07412 empirical companion and Monday's 2605.07588 training-surface extension rather than a fresh model, formalizes how the training-surface provenance chain composes with a tenant-policy-attestation manifest to give a single end-to-end signed reference from training-run checkpoint through agent-loader through tenant-policy gate, and reports the composition adds only a marginal additional overhead on top of the training-surface check measured in the Monday companion. A Tuesday Simon Willison note characterized the paper as the loader-verification line reaching its third documented extension within the May 16-19 four-day cluster, noting the three papers plus the original 2605.07241 framework now form a unified four-document reference set that the framework cohort's mid-June default-shipment commitment can cite as a single coherent surface. A Tuesday andrew.ooo reading observed the paper's reproduction harness extends the existing DeepMind plus Meta AI plus Anthropic plus Microsoft consolidated reference-implementation index to cover the tenant-policy-attestation manifest, closing the loop from training surface to deployment-time tenant gate.
